steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease two 8-inch round cake pans.
Whisk eggs in a small bowl; reserve about 1 tablespoon for brushing over dough. Whisk flour and baking powder together in another bowl.

Beat sugar and butter in a large bowl with an electric mixer until light and fluffy. Mix in beaten eggs, then stir in almond extract. Stir in flour mixture by hand using a sturdy spoon; dough will be stiff.
Press 1/2 of the dough into each prepared pan. Press almond slices into dough, then brush reserved egg over top.
Bake in the preheated oven until the top is golden brown, about 30 minutes. Let cool, then cut into wedges to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Boterkoek (Dutch Butter Cake)
raw_recipe.description: Boterkoek is a flat Dutch cake that's super buttery, moist, and full of sweet almond flavor from almond extract. This recipe makes two 8-inch cakes.
raw_recipe.name: Boterkoek (Dutch Butter Cake)

review.reviewBody: I am from Holland and can definitly say that this tastes pretty authentic. If you want perfectly authentic, put it aside and eat it the next day. Excellent! Yummm

As a 2nd generation Dutch immigrant to the US, I grew up eating and loving “almond cakes” that we bought from the Dutch Bakery in Ontario, CA, where there was a large population of Dutch people. This recipe is fantastic! I make these in muffin tins to copy the little cakes from my childhood. Using a muffin tin, butter the cups well and line each one with a circle of parchment paper for easy removal. Bake for 20 mins. They are perfect!

I am Dutch American (4th generation descendant of Dutch immigrants) and grew up enjoying boterkoek, yet I had never made it myself. I decided to give it a try, just in time for Christmas gatherings. I followed the recipe exactly and removed the cakes at 28 minutes, and they were waaay overdone and not quite as flavorful as I remembered. The finished product was definitely not something I would want to share at holiday gatherings. I tried again, this time adding 1 tsp vanilla extract and baked for 22 minutes. It came out perfect! I brought it to my family Christmas party tonight and received so many compliments from my Dutch relatives. Needless to say, there wasn't any left for me to take home!
I turned this recipe into bars. I doubled the batter and spread into parchment lined jelly roll pan. Pressed lots of almond slices into batter so that everything was covered. Omitted the egg wash.

I did do half vanilla and half almond extract which was plenty of almond for me. Also it all fit in one pan for a thicker cake. Delicious after doing this twice one pan is def the way to go so you dont have a flying saucer overdone cake

I have very good things to say about this recipe, it's easy, it's delicious and I cannot stop eating it. I only made one change, after reading the comments I followed their advice and I only used a teaspoon of almond extract and I used one teaspoon of vanilla extract. It definitely balances the taste. You can even tell that one teaspoon of almond extract is more than enough.

Used 4 eggs instead of baking powder for rising of cake, turned out great! Also 1/2 cup less of flour for less dense as per other suggestions. Topped with a self made peach puree and crushed almonds.Can also throw on peach slices on puree before crushed almonds or mango puree and slices for a tropical variation!

Delicious! I used 2 tsp of almond extract, and 1 tsp of lemon extract for extra flavour. I added 2 tbsp of milk to make it a little less dense,and a pinch of salt along with the flour and baking powder. Instead of brushing the egg on top I made a quick icing with powdered sugar, almond and lemon extract, and milk.

I cut recipe in half and baked in an 8" square pan. Mine was done at 25 minutes. Perfect little cake to go with tea. Easy to make and keeps well. 
Addendum: A month and a half later, I am actually CRAVING this cake right now. Thanks for sharing!

My favorite dessert in the Netherlands. I didn't add the almond extract or almonds because I don't really like them. The slices I had in the Netherlands didn't have almonds. I used 1/2 tsp of vanilla instead. It's the butter flavor I'm after and this hits the spot.

This is the best Almond Buttercake I have had, and I have eaten lots in Canada and the Netherlands! The only change I made was to bake in a 9x9 pan for 45 minutes and sprinkle the top with 100 grams of sliced almonds. Definitely a keeper, thanks!

This was very good! I did cut the almond flavoring to 1/2 Tbsp and added 1 tsp of vanilla. It was suggested in other reviews to leave it out overnight. But it was very hard to cut the next day at the potluck I took it to. It did taste good though! There were leftovers and I microwaved a slice for 1 minute -- delicious and perfect!
I made this for my Dutch husband and he loves it! The kids love it too! Easy and excellent recipe quick to make and clean up is easy too
I made to a tea and put it in a tart tin turned out perfect will be making it again

Made this for a going away party for my daughter who is headed to the Netherlands. It was a HUGE hit. Followed the recipe exactly other than 2 tsp almond and 1 tsp vanilla extract. Delicious with coffee. Making it for a second time today. Definite keeper.
So good with vanilla ice cream :)
I have made this delicious recipe today and it had came really good 😋. It may not be perfect to some people's eyes but it was my first time trying. And the result? So good and moist😋😋😋😋.
I supplemented a little cake flour in lieu of some all-purpose flour. With a Dutch family heritage, it is an homage to the pastries from that area. I already have plans to make it again.
This tastes exactly the same as the one my Dutch great grandmother used to make! Goes EXCELLENTLY WELL with coffee and a good conversation.

I thought it was great. A real favorite of my husbands. Really tasty and I didn’t even have the almonds or enough almond extract. I will make again with both. I just added vanilla to get it to the full tablespoon.
